reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every natural number n with n ≥ 3 and every real number κ with κ ≥ 4, make the following definitions. Let s = √κ, where √ is the real square root. Let G = O(n), the full group of real orthogonal n × n matrices, including both determinant signs, and let μ be the canonical normalized Haar probability measure on G. Write Q(O) for the real matrix underlying O ∈ G. Define measures on G by
ν₊ = 2 μ restricted to {O ∈ G : det Q(O) = 1},
ν₋ = 2 μ restricted to {O ∈ G : det Q(O) = −1}.
The factors 2 in these measure definitions are extended nonnegative real scalars.
For O ∈ G, define the real n × n matrices
A(O) = ((κ + 1)/2) Iₙ − ((κ − 1)/4)(Q(O) + Q(O)ᵀ),
C(O) = A(O)⁻¹,
and define γ(O) = multivariateGaussian(0, C(O)) on real n-dimensional Euclidean space. The matrix inverse here is the standard totalized matrix inverse. Precisely, the Gaussian constructor means the pushforward of canonical standard Gaussian measure by z ↦ 0 + Matrix.toEuclideanCLM(CFC.sqrt(C(O))) z; its covariance interpretation is the one supplied for positive semidefinite matrix arguments.
Let P₊ = ν₊.bind γ and P₋ = ν₋.bind γ, so these measures are obtained by integrating the displayed Gaussian measure γ(O) against the respective determinant-sign measures. Define the real number
δ = sup { |P₊.real(B) − P₋.real(B)| : B is a Borel measurable subset of real n-dimensional Euclidean space },
where P.real(B) is the extended nonnegative measure of B converted to a real number, and the supremum is the real sSup operator. Equivalently, the set whose sSup is taken consists of the real numbers z for which there exists a Borel measurable B with z = |P₊.real(B) − P₋.real(B)|.
Then both of the following weak inequalities hold:
(1/2) exp(−5n/s) ≤ ((s − 1)/(s + 1))ⁿ / (2 + 4ns/(s + 1)²),
((s − 1)/(s + 1))ⁿ / (2 + 4ns/(s + 1)²) ≤ δ.
Here n is converted to a real number in the exponential and the denominator, whereas the powers with exponent n are natural-number powers. Real division and inverse use their totalized Lean meanings. No attainment of the supremum, upper bound on δ, or additional universal parameter is part of this conclusion.
objects: s = Real.sqrt κ. G = Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ, identified with full O(n), and Q(O) denotes its underlying matrix. μ = Measure.haarMeasure(⊤ : PositiveCompacts G), the canonical normalized full-group Haar probability. νpos = 2 • (μ restricted to det Q(O) = 1) and νneg = 2 • (μ restricted to det Q(O) = −1), with 2 : ℝ≥0∞. A(O) = ((κ+1)/2) Iₙ − ((κ−1)/4)(Q(O)+Q(O)ᵀ). C(O) = A(O)⁻¹. γ is the map O ↦ multivariateGaussian(0,C(O)). Ppos = νpos.bind γ and Pneg = νneg.bind γ. δ is the real sSup of all absolute differences |Ppos.real B − Pneg.real B| over Borel measurable B. The intermediate expression F = (((s−1)/(s+1))^n)/(2+4(n:ℝ)s/(s+1)^2) is only a shorthand used in this reconstruction, not an additional Lean let.
domains: n : ℕ; κ,s,δ,z and all analytic expressions : ℝ. Fin n is the coordinate index set {0,…,n−1}. Q(O), A(O), C(O), Iₙ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ. O belongs to the full real orthogonal group with its matrix Borel measurable structure. μ,νpos,νneg are measures on that group. γ(O),Ppos,Pneg are measures on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), real n-dimensional Euclidean space with its standard Borel measurable space. B is a subset of that Euclidean space and is required to be Borel measurable. Measure scalars are extended nonnegative real numbers; Measure.real converts an event measure to ℝ. Matrix inversion, real division and real inverse are totalized; powers n and 2 are natural powers.
quantifiers: Universally quantify the implicit natural number n, then hn : 3 ≤ n, then the implicit real parameter κ, then hκ : 4 ≤ κ. These proof arguments supply the two hypotheses. Each displayed let subsequently defines an object rather than adding an independently quantified parameter. γ has a lambda-bound O ranging over the orthogonal group. Each determinant-sign set has its own set-bound O. In δ, z ranges over ℝ in the set comprehension and there exists a set B of Euclidean space satisfying MeasurableSet B and z = |Ppos.real B − Pneg.real B|. B and z are local to the supremum set, not fixed or universally quantified external parameters.
assumptions: The explicit hypotheses are precisely n ∈ ℕ with 3 ≤ n and κ ∈ ℝ with 4 ≤ κ. Orthogonality is carried by the type of O, Borel measurability by MeasurableSet B inside δ, and zero mean is fixed by definition. No additional hypothesis on a chosen O, event B, covariance matrix, or arbitrary constant appears. Normalized full-group Haar measure and the meaning of the Gaussian constructor are supplied by the approved definition context. In particular, the reconstruction does not add positive semidefiniteness as a hypothesis: it retains the exact Gaussian matrix argument and its supplied pushforward meaning.
conclusion: The conclusion is the conjunction L ≤ F ∧ F ≤ δ, where L = (1/2 : ℝ) * Real.exp (−(5*(n:ℝ))/s) and F = (((s−1)/(s+1))^n)/(2+4*(n:ℝ)*s/(s+1)^2). Both inequalities are non-strict. The exponent of exp is −5n/s, with division after the negative numerator. The power n applies to the full ratio (s−1)/(s+1). The full denominator of F is 2 + (4ns)/(s+1)^2. δ uses an absolute event difference and no additional factor 1/2. There is no assertion that the supremum is attained or any other bound or equality for δ.
scopes: All lets s,μ,νpos,νneg,γ,Ppos,Pneg,δ are nested in that order after both hypotheses and remain in scope for the entire final conjunction. s depends on κ; μ is defined on the group determined by n; νpos and νneg use that same μ. In γ, the inverse applies to the entire matrix ((κ+1)/2)•Iₙ − ((κ−1)/4)•(Q(O)+Q(O)ᵀ), not to an individual summand. The scalar ((κ−1)/4) multiplies the sum of Q(O) and its transpose. Ppos and Pneg integrate the same γ against different determinant restrictions. In δ, the existential B has scope over the conjunction MeasurableSet B ∧ z = |Ppos.real B − Pneg.real B|. The absolute value encloses the whole real-valued measure difference. Parentheses in the final inequalities identify the same F on their adjacent sides.
constant_dependencies: The only free mathematical parameters are n and κ under their displayed lower bounds. s depends only on κ. G,Q,Iₙ,μ,νpos,νneg depend on n and not κ; Q also takes the local argument O. A,C,γ depend on n and κ, and their evaluations additionally on O. Ppos,Pneg,δ,L,F depend on n and κ, with L and F using κ through s. All numerical constants are fixed exactly as displayed: lower thresholds 3 and 4; zero Gaussian mean; determinant signs 1 and −1; factor 2 for each restricted Haar measure; coefficients (κ+1)/2 and (κ−1)/4; prefactor 1/2 and exponent coefficient 5 in L; shifts −1 and +1 in the ratio; additive denominator constant 2, multiplier 4, and denominator square in F. No unspecified multiplicative constant, asymptotic qualification, or additional dimension-independent choice is quantified.
